page_title: Moving from orchestration to choreography - Part 3

sources.entry: Moving from orchestration to choreography - By Olivier Jauze, March 2021. Michelin's journey from BPM orchestration to event-driven choreography. It's the first of a series and continues with part 2 and part 3.

summary.title: Moving from orchestration to choreography - Part 3
summary.one_liner: Michelin's final part of the series shares team perspectives (tech lead, software engineer, DevOps, team lead) on replacing a BPM orchestration system with a Kafka Streams event-driven microservice choreography, and the lessons learned.
keywords: kafka streams error handling dead letter queue
kafka streams health probes readiness liveness
takeaways: Event-driven choreography needs a mindset shift; topology concepts must be understood by non-technical team members too, and expect rework early on.
Build a CI/CD pipeline and automation from day one, with automated unit tests and code coverage standards for many microservices.
Use a shared error-handling framework and an abstraction layer (e.g., a base StreamInitializer) so Kafka Streams apps don't crash and new microservices ship quickly.
Expose observability early: Prometheus/Grafana metrics across Kafka, Kubernetes and Kafka Streams were needed to diagnose rebalances and stuck services.
Retaining events in Kafka lets you replay production traffic into test environments to compare new and old versions of a stream.
summary.summary: This final article in Michelin's series gives four team viewpoints: tech lead, software engineer, DevOps and team lead, on moving order orchestration from a BPM product to Kafka Streams microservices. The software engineer section includes code for a generic DLQ error-handling step, a StreamInitializer base class with health endpoints, and a topology test base class. The DevOps section covers monitoring, topic and Kafka Connect provisioning, and replicating production events to a test environment. The article ends with key takeaways on event-driven design, CI/CD, observability and roadmaps.
